doc.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Sterling Brown sneaking jazz into Howard University
summary: Per Billy Taylor's talk, Sterling Brown slipped jazz lessons into class at Howard, where black colleges frowned on jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I was talking to Billy Taylor downstairs and we were talking about Howard University. And he was telling me they have a wonderful jazz music program and of course Howard Law School was where Brown v. Board came out of, but before that when Sterling Brown, the poet, the expert on the blues, was teaching at Howard — he told me this years ago — Howard, like several other all-black colleges, would not allow jazz because it came from bad origins. So Sterling Brown would bring in a Milhaud piece, Stravinsky’s “Ragtime” and then he’d say to the students, “now let me show you where they learned that.” So then he snuck in the jazz lesson.
I see. He had to go through the back door.
